newsitem.title: USA: Oil spill stops Alaska tanker loadings.
newsitem.headline: Oil spill stops Alaska tanker loadings.

text.p: Loading of oil tankers was halted at the Prince William Sound terminal of the trans-Alaska pipeline on Friday after workers spotted an oil slick, company and state officials said.
The patchy oil sheens, which state observers said included a streak about a half mile (0.8 km) long and several yards (metres) wide, was discovered on Friday morning.

A spokesman for Alyeska Pipeline Service Co., the consortium that operates the 800-mile (1,280 km) pipeline and its Valdez marine terminal, said investigators had not yet pinpointed the source of the oil leak.
"We're aggressively stating that we do not know where it's coming from," Alyeska spokesman Mike Abbott said.
Docked at the terminal port were three tankers, the Overseas Ohio, Arco Fairbanks and Arco Spirit, Alyeska said. The Overseas Ohio was being operated under charter for British Petroleum, Abbott said.
Alyeska crew have started to skim the spilled oil and have set out boom to collect it, with extra boom set out near a local duck-nesting area as a precaution, the company said.

State and federal observers who flew over the site saw separate sheens, including light patches at the terminal and heavier sheens, inclding the half-mile streak, offshore, the Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) said.
The spilled oil appears to be old, making detection of its source more difficult, said Leslie Pearson, acting on-scene cleanup coordinator for DEC.
Although the oil was bubbling up next to the Overseas Ohio, divers who checked the vessel on Friday found no cracks or leaks, she said. More dives were scheduled for later, she said.
"I'm not convinced yet that it's coming from the Overseas Ohio," she said. "Because it's weathered product, I'm leaning towards perhaps another source."
The Overseas Ohio is a double-hulled vessel, "which makes me even more suspicious that it would be from another source," she said.
A possible culprit could be the terminal's ballast-water-treatment plant, which has an outfall near the berthed vessels, Pearson said.
The trans-Alaska pipeline transports about 1.4 million barrels of oil daily, on average.
Alyeska is a consortium owned by seven oil companies with interests on Alaska's North Slope.
Major owners are British Petroleum, Atlantic Richfield and Exxon. Mobil, Unocal , Amerada Hess and Phillips Petroleum own minor shares.
